name: ppo-anchor-tiebreak-v1
status: amended after review and BEFORE any tie-break run (see amendments); written AFTER the pilot results were read (declared reading: a tie between E0 and A1)
label: descriptive tie-break between E0 and A1 to choose the arm for the confirmation; no confirmatory claim; the Room 1 set is a development set (aggregates only); the Room 1 v2 set and the Room 2 v2 set are never read
question: The PPO anchor pilot (config/ppo-anchor-pilot.json, results in docs/results/ppo-anchor-pilot.json) read as a tie between E0 (PPO's entropy bonus turned off) and A1 (anchor lambda 1). With 4 runs per arm the difference is inside the noise. Which of the two do we carry into the confirmation on the fresh Room 1 v2 set?

tie_choice_record.recorded_as: a choice, not a result (as config/ppo-anchor-pilot.json declares for a tie)
tie_choice_record.declared_tie_break: by simplicity and cost (config/ppo-anchor-pilot.json, decision_branches.reading_them_together (d)); this points to E0: one flag instead of donor recordings, anchor code and donor checkpoints, and 79 to 82 minutes per run for E0 against 104 minutes for A1-k3, the only A1 run of the pilot that was not resumed (3 side by side, 10 threads)
tie_choice_record.decision: the owner chose to carry E0 forward as the default and to run this small tie-break before the confirmation, because the confirmation as declared compares the chosen arm with the control only and the fresh v2 set can be used once (review verdict on the pilot results, 2026-09-29, findings F4 to F6 and the recommendation after F7)
tie_choice_record.what_the_pilot_shows_about_E0_against_A1: per-run one-unit drops E0 0.010, 0.116, 0.305, 0.362 and A1 0.106, 0.021, 0.086, 0.058 (clones k0 to k3); median 0.2105 against 0.0722; E0 above 0.25 in 2 of 4 runs, A1 in 0 of 4 (exact two-sided p about 0.43 on those counts); the E0 loss appears late (median drop 0.066, 0.118, 0.205, 0.210 at 200k, 300k, 400k, 500k against 0.035 to 0.072 for A1) and depends on the clone (on clone k2 E0 beats A1 at all 5 checkpoints)

arms.not_rerun: A10 (it held Room 1 but cost Room 2 in 2 of 4 finals and is not a candidate) and the control (the SD-k PPO runs, not rerun)

held_fixed.command: exactly the pilot's command for the same arm and k (config/campaign-ppo-anchor-train.json), with only --seed and --run-dir changed; the generator checks this mechanically
held_fixed.evaluation: identical to the pilot: Room 1 held-out (scripts/evaluate_heldout.py --starts config/heldout_starts.json --repeats 1 --seed 20260920) at every 100k checkpoint (5 per run), Room 2 canonical (scripts/evaluate_checkpoint.py, 50 episodes, seed 20260924, rew-v2, shaping 2.0) on the final, Room 2 v1 held-out (config/heldout_starts-room2.json, seed 20260922) on the final
held_fixed.floors: clone floor 0.142 and final floor 0.2046 (docs/results/retention-pilot.json); the one-unit drop (clone - 500k) / (donor before - 0.142), the same formula as the pilot
held_fixed.threads: 10 torch threads, set explicitly and recorded by run_overnight.py, 3 game copies side by side, memory floor 2.5 GB, as in the pilot

new_runs.count: 8: E0 and A1 for k = 0 to 3 (clone SD-k)
new_runs.seeds: PPO seed 50 + k (the pilot used 40 + k); for A1 the anchor split seed k and anchor batch seed k are unchanged (the same 19 fitted and 6 held-back episodes, the same anchor batch schedule); only the PPO sampling randomness is new
new_runs.order: interleaved A1-k0, E0-k0, A1-k1, E0-k1, A1-k2, E0-k2, A1-k3, E0-k3 so neither arm is systematically run first or last

running.training: 8 runs side by side, 3 at a time on the three game copies (run_overnight.py --copy), 240 minutes per run (the limit only catches hangs; in the pilot with 3 side by side E0 took 79 to 82 minutes, A1-k3 104 beside two E0 runs, and the A10 runs up to 177 of 180 beside two other anchored runs; A1 costs the same as A10, and a timed-out A1 run would be killed and resumed, recreating the pilot's confound that only A1 runs were resumed)
running.failure_policy: a run that ends not ok after the runner's one resume, or that has to be stopped by hand, is rerun from scratch with the same seed in a new folder (runs/train/ppo-tiebreak-<arm>-k<k>-rerun<n>) through a committed plan amendment, and reported by name with the failed attempt; the rule is applied only to 8 complete runs per arm; a run that the runner resumed once and that then finished ok counts, and is reported by name with its replayed anchor.csv rows
running.evaluation: side by side on the three copies at 10 threads, 56 evaluations
running.interruption: a run that is killed and resumed is valid but not bit-identical; the analyzer reports every resumed run by name and its replayed anchor.csv rows
running.v2_sets_unread: the plan generator and the analyzer refuse any command or result that names config/heldout_starts-room1-v2.json or config/heldout_starts-room2-v2.json
running.owner_cutoff: 2026-09-30 10:00 London time (BST): do not start further jobs at or after this cutoff; the training plan stop_time also prevents starting a run whose declared limit extends beyond it

measurements.primary: each new run's Room 1 held-out route-macro at every 100k checkpoint and its one-unit drop, pooled with the pilot's E0 and A1 runs (8 per arm)
measurements.descriptive_only: Room 2 canonical finals and Room 2 v1 held-out finals (pooled medians against the M-k median 0.8176), the per-clone comparison (E0 minus A1 on the same clone, pilot and new seed), the mean drop over the 200k to 500k checkpoints, the number of runs with a drop above 0.25 at any checkpoint, and each arm's pilot and new batch separately

decision_rule.pooling: 8 runs per arm: the pilot's four (PPO seeds 40 to 43, from docs/results/ppo-anchor-pilot.json) and these four (PPO seeds 50 to 53); each run's one-unit drop from its own Room 1 held-out curve
decision_rule.rule: Carry E0 forward unless BOTH hold: (1) at least 3 more E0 runs than A1 runs have a one-unit drop ABOVE 0.25 (counted over the 8 pooled runs of each arm), and (2) E0's pooled median drop is MORE THAN 0.10 above A1's pooled median drop. If both hold, carry A1 forward. Otherwise carry E0 forward, the declared tie-break (simplicity and cost). The comparisons are strict where written above and more than, and at least 3 is inclusive.
decision_rule.why_these_thresholds: set after the pilot results were read (post hoc, and stated as such). The pilot alone already gives a count gap of 2 (E0 2 of 4 above 0.25, A1 0 of 4) and a median gap of 0.138, so the COUNT condition needs only one more net bad E0 run; the MEDIAN condition is what does the work. Holding the pilot's runs fixed and assuming the new A1 runs behave like the pilot's: 0 new E0 runs above 0.25 gives E0; 1 gives a median gap of about 0.04, so E0; 2 or more gives a median gap of about 0.12 to 0.14, so A1. The rule therefore switches to A1 only if the new batch repeats the pilot's pattern, about half of E0's runs losing more than a quarter of the margin. The per-run condition is there because a median of 4 hides a split (review finding F7). The median gap is compared after rounding to 6 decimals, so an exact 0.10 is not more than 0.10.
decision_rule.not_in_the_rule: Room 2 measures, randomness and everything under measurements.descriptive_only are reported and cannot move the decision. Whichever arm the rule names (E0 or A1), the analyzer applies the pilot's Room 2 conditions to its 8 pooled runs (Room 2 v1 median at least 0.7676, and at least 6 of 8 canonical finals at 45 or more); a failure requires review and a recorded choice by the owner before the confirmation is planned, and does not change the rule's answer
decision_rule.inputs_pinned: the pilot's drops come from docs/results/ppo-anchor-pilot.json, pinned in the analyzer by its text sha256 fbbf136858b4d6b7f198d705814dee7347c9bed5aa1f20c00a3ab8758c6911ea; the analyzer refuses if it differs, checks that each new run's manifest records seed 50 + k and the planned clone, and requires exactly 5 Room 1 checkpoints per run; the evaluation plan generator refuses a run whose latest.zip (used for the Room 2 finals) is not the same policy as its step_000501760.zip (used for the Room 1 final)
decision_rule.no_other_outcome: no arm is picked after the fact; both arms' pooled figures are reported whatever the rule says

declared_confounds: The 8 runs per arm are not 8 independent draws: they come from only 4 clones (two PPO seeds each), and E0's large drops were on clones k1 and k3, so a clone effect can count twice in the pooled counts. This is accepted on purpose: whether E0 is reliable across these starting policies is the question, and a clone-level rule on 4 clones would have almost no power; every clone and batch is reported separately.

Each clone's Room 1 starting point is a single 200-start measurement, shared by all four runs on that clone (two arms, two seeds). Its noise is roughly 0.056 in drop units and moves those runs together, including across the 0.25 line; E0-k1's 0.305 is about one such unit above 0.25.

A1's two runs per clone share more randomness than E0's: the new A1 runs reuse the pilot's anchor split seed and anchor batch seed (only the PPO seed is new), so A1's seed-to-seed spread may look smaller partly by construction.
The rule's thresholds were set after the pilot results were read.

The pilot and the tie-break batches ran at different times; the pilot's A1-k0, A1-k1 and A1-k2 were resumed once (two sessions, commits 54c9556 then 9a3ee81, valid but not bit-identical to an uninterrupted run), the new runs should not be; both batches are reported separately as well as pooled.

The anchor frames lie within a few pixels of most Room 1 test starts (coverage-ceiling descriptive: 59% to 76% within 4 px), so the anchor rehearses Room 1 near the test's paths; E0 does not. Legitimate for retention, and stated whenever A1 and E0 are compared.
ent_coef 0 also removes exploration pressure in Room 2, which may slow Room 2 learning; E0's Room 2 measures show it.
Four donors, all from one recipe (Phase 3B arm B); the Room 1 development set has been used by Phase 3B and five pilots.
